topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: To mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band, adaptive beamforming techniques with real-time optimization frameworks should be employed. These techniques consider factors like interference mitigation and user distribution per beam, allowing multibeam satellite systems to adapt to changing channel conditions. The use of high-gain beams in mmWave bands limits effective beam spread, changing selectivity properties. Interference mitigation techniques provide significant spectral efficiency gains but with a trade-off between beamforming granularity and interference reduction.
reference_context: The reference context provides numerical results for a multiband single beam satellite system operating in the Ka band, where a maximum difference of 13 dB is observed between user channel gains within a beam due to rainy weather conditions. The use of narrower beams in higher frequency bands limits the effective spread of rays and changes the selectivity properties of beamformed equivalent channels.
